solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like some 19th-century novels, a kind since abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Novels of a type that has long since gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like it describes the kind of novel, but it signals rearranging the letters of A KIND SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens wrote many Victorian novels, so the adjective formed from his name describes them.

clue.text: Like a nobleman's double, taking in Commons at first

indicators.note: taking in means one piece swallows another, holding it inside

parts.note: double means twofold, dual

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word Commons

explanation.surface: A nobleman's double sits in the House of Commons, as if a peer had a lookalike among the elected members.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal is the adjective for a duke, the highest rank of British nobleman.

clue.text: Safekeeping of satin cover on ground

indicators.note: ground as the past of grind means crushed and broken up, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Protecting a satin cover by laying it on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as a noun to lay the cover on, but it is the past tense of grind, signalling an anagram of SATIN COVER ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation is the preservation and protection of something, a synonym for keeping it safe.

clue.text: Winged statue thus about to be erected?

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting something stands it upright, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: thus means so, in that way
re means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A statue of a winged figure is about to be put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be erected' turns SORE upside down in the down light. The famous Eros statue stands in London's Piccadilly Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The statue of the winged archer atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.

clue.text: Tried hard to get supper finally in oven

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for oven

parts.note: a stove is a cooker or oven

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word supper

explanation.surface: Someone made a great effort to get the supper into the oven at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made a great effort.

clue.text: Correctness of notes on church office

parts.note: A and C are musical notes
a curacy is the office or post of a curate in the church

explanation.surface: Getting the notes right during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' suggests a service, but here it is a post held, the curacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy means freedom from error, the same idea as being correct.

clue.text: Manage publicity initially required in small country?

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for a small country

parts.note: a ministate is a very small sovereign country

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word required

explanation.surface: Is publicity needed to run a tiny nation?
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to run or direct affairs, a close synonym of managing.

clue.text: Report of senior officer — a bit of a nut!

indicators.note: report means something heard, so the answer sounds like the officer's title when spoken

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A report about a senior officer who is somewhat crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nut' seems to call the colonel eccentric, but it defines the edible inner part of a nut; colonel is said 'kernel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel is the soft edible seed inside a nut's shell, literally part of it.

clue.text: Profile of Conservative leader travelling from place to place

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word Conservative

parts.note: a band travelling from place to place is on tour

explanation.surface: A sketch of a Tory party leader out campaigning around the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative leader' suggests a politician, but it only supplies C.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is an outline or silhouette, which is one sense of profile.

clue.text: Be concerned about daughter in service unit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for being concerned goes round the letter

parts.note: to care is to be concerned

explanation.surface: Worrying about one's daughter who is in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained personnel forming a unit in the armed services.

clue.text: Lecherous look making us stagger backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the word for stagger is read from right to left

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: A lascivious glance that makes us reel back in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive or lustful sideways glance.

clue.text: An account giving rise to extreme distaste

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a version is an account or telling of events

explanation.surface: A story that leads to a strong dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or repugnance felt towards something.

clue.text: Spanish queen, the first murder victim in one's city?

indicators.note: in places the victim inside the other letters

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I'S, the letters IS
LA is Los Angeles, a US city
in Genesis, Abel was killed by Cain, the first murder

explanation.surface: A Spanish queen is the first person murdered in one's own city.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella I of Castile was the Spanish queen who sponsored Columbus's voyage.

clue.text: Duke introducing American composer, a rich man

indicators.note: introducing means placing the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: Charles Ives was a modernist American composer

explanation.surface: A duke presents an American composer to a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in Jesus's parable of the rich man and Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives, Latin for rich, became the name for the wealthy man in the Lazarus parable, hence any rich man.

clue.text: Shortage of food ultimately overwhelming planet

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter sits over the word for planet
ultimately points to the closing letter of the word food

parts.note: Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: A lack of food is finally swamping the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, a synonym for shortage.

clue.text: Head of class unwell, nursing start of horrible cold

indicators.note: nursing means holding something close, so the letter goes inside
head of points to the opening letter of the word class

parts.note: ill means unwell

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the word horrible

explanation.surface: The class head is off sick, looking after a nasty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the illness being nursed, but it is the definition, as a noun meaning chilliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a coldness in the air or a feverish cold, so it can stand for cold.

clue.text: Divided paintings briefly kept in outhouse

indicators.note: kept in means placed inside the word for an outhouse

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for paintings loses its last letter

parts.note: paintings are art

explanation.surface: Pictures stored in a garden shed for a short time, then split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared means split between people, as when a cake is divided.

clue.text: Hunt a boa slithering around German motorway

indicators.note: the snake slithering around suggests letters moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Chasing a boa constrictor that is slithering over a German road.
explanation.definitionFit: Autobahn is the German word for a high-speed national road, a motorway.

clue.text: Move domestic animals from the east?

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so backwards

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: Moving pets in from eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a move, a measure taken, as in taking the next move.

clue.text: Shame about conclusion of padre's godliness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shame goes round the letter

parts.note: shame as in 'what a shame' means pity

indicators.note: conclusion of points to the closing letter of the word padre

explanation.surface: A pity about how the padre's devotion ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is devout religious reverence, the same quality as godliness.

clue.text: Pulpit used by Uppingham boys

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pulpit used by pupils at Uppingham School.
explanation.walkthrough: Uppingham is an English private school in Rutland.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early Christian churches.

clue.text: Internet pest missing start of leisurely walk

indicators.note: missing start of means the word for walk loses its first letter

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: An online nuisance who skips the start of a relaxed stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll posts provocative messages online to upset others, a common internet nuisance.

clue.text: Go berserk — hit boy attendant

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a page is a boy attendant, as at a wedding or hotel

explanation.surface: Someone runs wild and strikes a young attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and out of control, as one does when berserk.

clue.text: Graciously departs in old cab by Cambs cathedral

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for an old cab

parts.note: a hansom was a horse-drawn two-wheeled cab
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone leaves politely in a vintage cab near Ely Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambs is the short form of Cambridgeshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsomely can mean generously or in a gracious, fine manner.
